title: pteridium aquilinum subsp. esculentum
intro: Pteridium aquilinum subsp. esculentum, commonly known as bracken, is a type of fern that grows in many parts of the world. It has been reported to have several health benefits, including reducing inflammation, improving digestion, and acting as an antioxidant. The therapeutic actions of bracken are attributed to its bioactive constituents, which include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and sesquiterpene lactones, that have anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and anticancer properties. However, excessive consumption of bracken can be toxic due to the presence of a carcinogenic compound called ptaquiloside, which highlights the need for proper identification and use of this plant.
